hypothesis: A validation-only structural certificate admits bounded affine scalar-fission loops whose enclosing-row exit is split by ordinary LV into row.exit -> a dedicated empty forwarding block -> exit. Direct exits remain supported. This removes the demonstrated t000027 checker obstruction without changing LLVM transformations, legality/admission, profitability, the C execution harness, the 117 immutable inputs or any FP/errno contract.
semantics: In BOTH original and transformed IR, the enclosing certificate retains the unsigned 1<=rows<=4 and 1<=n<=65 entry guard, exact entry polarity and outer.ph/outer/inner.ph edges, zero-based row PHI, row.next=row+1, rows.done=(row.next==rows) and false backedge to outer. The exact true successor of br i1 %rows.done is either exit, or a block discovered from that CFG edge. The latter must have exactly the single incoming row.exit edge and contain only br label %exit after ignoring blank/comment lines and metadata attachments. No PHI, pure arithmetic, load, store, call or other work is admitted. Final exit must have exactly entry and the checked direct/forwarded predecessor. This rejects extra predecessors, guard/exit bypasses, wrong conditions/polarity/backedges/destinations, conditional hops, cycles and additional hops; predecessor comments and block spelling are not trusted. Incoming-edge scans now count label operands on unexpected switch/invoke terminators as well, so they cannot conceal an extra predecessor. The finite forward producer DAG, preserved original controls and instructions, sole exiting latch, exact consumer entry, unique SSA definitions and ordered arithmetic expansion templates are unchanged. The enclosing expansion still spans outer.ph then outer, with checked guard/row bounds proving N=n and origin=row+5. No new count-expression template is accepted. Ordinal/actual-completed/export placement and edges, one-way removal of integer nowrap flags, metadata/prefix/comment/placement checks, actual participant P and empty-stream bypass remain intact. Modular relational early-exit siblings cannot use n or a storage witness as actual N. New production-checker positives/negatives operate on retained IR only and are not executable correctness evidence. Mandatory verification must transform original scalar IR with real opt after one and two ordinary LV invocations and compare actual code against original IR AND independent C formulas, including exact stage/participant/vector/tail visits, null zero entry, enclosing scratch reuse and reduction carry, masks, tails, aliases/future-row aliases, canaries, inactive invalid operands, ordered FP bits and signed zero. Strict and explicitly enabled fission FP reordering remain separate policies without extra assumptions.
costs: Validation-only: no target scratch allocation/traffic, input reread, recomputation, producer duplication, runtime guard, profitability or compiler analysis change. The checker adds a constant-size row-exit certificate and a constant number of linear scans of fixture instruction/label operands. Existing SSA maps and bounded arithmetic/CFG templates remain; no solver, arbitrary path enumeration or general exit-walking machinery is added. Only one dedicated empty forwarding hop is accepted. Underlying scratch is unchanged: entry allocation of M times unique contribution allocation sizes plus padding, capped at the existing 65536-byte per-candidate ceiling and signed pointer-index bound. At M=65, mixed fixtures account for 1044 bytes (65*i32+65*double+65*float plus 4 padding bytes), with 16*N logical store bytes and 16*N load bytes, or 16*P each for compact streams. Enclosing rows reuse 784 accounted bytes (65*i32+65*double plus padding), with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row, without multiplying capacity by rows. Scalar i32 boundary fixtures reserve 4/1020/65536 bytes at M=1/255/16384 and transfer 8*N total bytes (131072 at the ceiling). Noncanonical producers retain an ordinal PHI, one unit latch increment and completed export; compaction retains P and its empty guard. No original-input rereads, contribution recomputation, mask arrays, new alias/SCEV versioning guards, dynamic or unbounded storage are added. Physical stack traffic, register pressure, RVV execution and speedup remain unmeasured.
